The S&P 500 rose 0.86%, the Nasdaq gained 0.96%, and the Dow added 0.98% on Friday, extending a rebound in US equities.
Brent crude retreated from recent multi-month highs to around $104.60, with the oil pullback helping to support Friday's equity gains.
A hotter-than-expected August CPI print reinforced roughly 90% market-implied odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike at next week's meeting.
Tech and AI-related hardware names Dell Technologies (DELL), Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), and HP (HPQ) advanced, with Dell reaching a record high after Oracle (ORCL)'s earnings beat.
The combination of elevated inflation relative to wage growth and tight energy markets underscored risks of higher-for-longer interest rates and a potential winter energy strain.
Monday's US macro calendar is light, featuring minor housing data releases alongside 3- and 6-month Treasury bill auctions.
Monday's earnings slate is focused on small caps including Hain Celestial (HAIN), RF Industries (RFIL), Coda Octopus (CODA), and Dave & Buster's (PLAY).
Investors are looking ahead to Wednesday's US retail sales report and the Federal Reserve's widely expected rate hike next week as key catalysts.
Markets also monitored potential weekend geopolitical developments in the Middle East and Russian grain exports for possible impacts on energy and food prices.
